title: The normalized reduced integral presentation exists and is unique
statement:
In the situation of [prop-rational-descent], the point-count zeta
series has a unique
normalized reduced
integral presentation: there are unique $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$ with
$A(0)=B(0)=1$, $\gcd(A,B)=1$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$, and
$Z(X_0,T)=A(T)/B(T)$.
The fraction identity is interpreted as a Taylor-series identity at $T=0$, in the sense of [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction].

proof.text: Put $Z=Z(X_0,T)$ for the point-count series in the hypotheses. Apply [prop-weil-zeta-integral-rational], whose hypothesis is exactly the same situation of [prop-rational-descent] as here. It gives $Z\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T)$: thus $Z$ has integer coefficients, constant coefficient one, and is rational over $\mathbf Q$. These are all the hypotheses needed in the next step.

source.place: Proof, the integrality/rationality input followed by Fatou and the normalized-fraction definition

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-integral-rational-series] to this $Z$. Its hypotheses are precisely the three conclusions of step 1. Its conclusion supplies a unique pair $(A,B)$ of polynomials in $\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfying $A(0)=B(0)=1$, coprimality in $\mathbf Q[T]$, and $BZ=A$ as an identity in $\mathbf Z[[T]]$. In particular this gives uniqueness of the pair, with both constant coefficients normalized, rather than merely uniqueness up to a common scalar.

source.place: Proof, the integrality/rationality input followed by Fatou and the normalized-fraction definition

proof.text: By [def-weil-normalized-integral-fraction], the Taylor-series identity $Z(T)=A(T)/B(T)$ in the assertion means exactly $BZ=A$ with the polynomials regarded as formal power series. Thus the conditions in step 2 are exactly the defining conditions in the assertion. The same equivalence applies to any candidate pair $(A_2,B_2)$, so the existence and uniqueness in step 2 give both existence and uniqueness required here.
